# debug-container
[![Artifact Hub](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://artifacthub.io/badge/repository/techwolf12-debug-container)](https://artifacthub.io/packages/search?repo=techwolf12-debug-container)

Debug docker container that has a few tools for k8s debugging.  
Feel free to open a issue/PR if you want a tool in here.

## Tools

### Node specific
| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `pid2pod <pid>` | Find the pod that owns a PID during a node debug session |
| `inotify-consumers` | List the top inotify consumers on the node |
| `ps` | Check processes on the node |
| `htop` | Interactive process and resource viewer |

### DNS & connectivity
| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dig` / `nslookup` / `host` | DNS resolution debugging (CoreDNS/kube-dns, service discovery) |
| `ping` | Basic ICMP reachability check |
| `nc` | Test whether a service/port is reachable (netcat) |
| `mtr` | Combined traceroute + ping for path and latency analysis |
| `tcpdump` | Packet capture for network path debugging |
| `ss` / `ip` | Modern socket and interface inspection (iproute2) |
| `curl` | The must-have for any debug container, making random network requests inside your container |
| `grpc-client-cli` | For making gRPC requests |
| `openssl` | Inspect TLS certs, e.g. `openssl s_client -connect host:443` |

### Performance & stress testing
| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `iperf` | Network performance testing |
| `speedtest-cli` | Test internet network speed |
| `ab` | Apache Benchmark for HTTP load testing |
| `fio` | Disk I/O benchmarking |
| `stress-ng` | CPU/memory/IO stress testing to reproduce resource issues |

### Process & file inspection
| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `lsof` | List open files, sockets and ports |
| `strace` | Trace syscalls of a running/started process |
| `socat` | Port forwarding and protocol bridging |
| `vim` | Edit files and configs during debugging |

### Database & cache clients
| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `psql` | PostgreSQL client for connectivity testing |
| `mysql` | MySQL/MariaDB client for connectivity testing |
| `redis-cli` | Redis client for connectivity testing |

### Cluster & data tools
| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `kubectl` | Query the cluster API from inside a pod (with a mounted service account token) |
| `yq` | YAML processor (jq for YAML/k8s manifests) |
| `jq` | JSON processor |
| `nmap` | Port scanning |
| `google-cloud-cli` | CLI for talking to GCloud |

## Running the container

The image is available at `ghcr.io/techwolf12/debug-container:latest`.

### Quick throwaway pod

Spins up a pod, drops you into a shell, and deletes it on exit.

```bash
kubectl run techwolf12-debug \
  --rm -it --restart=Never \
  --image-pull-policy=Always \
  --image=ghcr.io/techwolf12/debug-container:latest \
  -- /bin/bash
```

### Debug a specific node

Runs a privileged pod in the node's namespaces to debug the host itself.

```bash
kubectl debug -it node/NODE_NAME \
  --image-pull-policy=Always \
  --image=ghcr.io/techwolf12/debug-container:latest
```

### Debug an existing pod (ephemeral container)

Attaches to a running pod, sharing its network and (optionally) process namespace,
without restarting it.

```bash
kubectl debug -it POD_NAME \
  --image=ghcr.io/techwolf12/debug-container:latest \
  --target=CONTAINER_NAME \
  --share-processes
```

### With a kubectl service account token

To use the bundled `kubectl` against the cluster API, run the pod with a service
account that has the permissions you need. The token, CA cert and API endpoint are
mounted automatically, so `kubectl` works with no extra config.

```bash
kubectl run techwolf12-debug \
  --rm -it --restart=Never \
  --image-pull-policy=Always \
  --image=ghcr.io/techwolf12/debug-container:latest \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"SERVICE_ACCOUNT_NAME"}}' \
  -- /bin/bash
```

> [!CAUTION]
> Bind the service account to only the RBAC it needs as the pod can do anything the
> service account is allowed to do.

### Locally with Docker

Handy for trying out the tooling without a cluster.

```bash
docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/techwolf12/debug-container:latest /bin/bash
```
